newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SAIL sets investment goal.
newsitem.headline: India's SAIL sets investment goal.

text.p: State-run Steel Authority of India Ltd (SAIL) plans to invest 150 billion rupees on modernisation and expansion over the next five years, the government said on Thursday.
SAIL has invested 200 billion rupees in modernisation and expansion since 1986, it said in a statement.
"Since 1986, SAIL has spent over 200 billion rupees on modernisation and update of its plants," the statement said.
"It plans to invest another approximately 150 billion on update, addition, modification and replacement (AMR) schemes during the Ninth Plan," it said.
The government's Ninth Plan covers a five-year period starting on April 1, 1997.
The modernisation of its plants would help SAIL reduce production costs, the statement said.
"The yield of saleable steel from liquid steel will improve substantially," it said.
The production cost at its Rourkela steel plant in the eastern state of Orissa would come cown by 1,100 rupees per tonne, the statement said.

It said that once the modernisation programme was completed, the annual capacity of its Durgapur steel plant in the eastern state of Bihar would be 1.87 million tonnes of crude steel, up from 800,000 tonnes.
